feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector roles: the positioning is clear, experience progression is logical, and the scope feels substantive. It reads professionally, but impact would improve with tighter prioritization, fewer repeated themes, and more consistently quantified outcomes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: strong progression at NACo into senior ownership of web, analytics, governance, multimedia, and strategy.  
- Good credibility signals: named platforms/tools, large-scale website metrics, team/channel scope, and concrete project examples.  
- Writing is polished overall: concise, professional tone with strong domain alignment for digital platform and communications leadership roles.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to create a sharper, less repetitive structure.  
- Add more outcome-focused metrics beyond activity/scope, especially for freelance work and earlier roles: e.g., efficiency gains, engagement lifts, adoption, revenue/support impact.  
- Fix style consistency issues: “organization-wide” vs. “organization’s,” “front-end” vs. other hyphenation choices, and list punctuation around “web, email, social, and multimedia” (serial comma usage varies). No obvious misspellings or major grammar errors; “10×20-foot” may be clearer as “10 x 20-foot” or “10-by-20-foot.”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and sector focus, but it reads slightly generic and repeats several competency areas already covered elsewhere. It would be stronger with one concrete scale signal and tighter phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “building the platforms” with more direct leadership language like “leading” or “delivering.”
- Add one proof point from recent experience, e.g., “10,000+ page Drupal migration” or “3.5M annual page views,” to increase impact.
- Tighten the service list to the most differentiating themes: web modernization, governance, analytics, and AI-enabled discovery.
- Consider aligning with the subtitle: “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader” for a more cohesive header.

Possible rewrite:
Digital platform and communications systems leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing public-sector web ecosystems, governance models and content operations. Led enterprise Drupal transformation for a 10,000+ page site serving 3.5M annual page views, while building analytics infrastructure, editorial systems and AI-enabled discovery experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Analytics infrastructure,” “editorial systems,” “multimedia production,” and “AI-enabled user experiences” are already echoed heavily in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be more effective if tightened, made more distinctive, and phrased with parallel structure.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, cleaner competency labels with consistent noun phrasing; avoid “and”/“&” style mixing.
- Emphasize highest-value, recent strengths: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI search, automation, and multimedia operations.
- Consider this rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, dashboards, and reporting infrastructure • Cross-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- If space is tight, replace “Cross-channel communications operations” with “Content operations leadership” for sharper differentiation.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “AI-enabled search,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “multimedia production” are already prominent in the header, Topline Skills, and recent roles.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” also repeats language used in the header and work experience.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it largely repeats achievements already covered in recent roles. Tightening the phrasing and framing these as selected outcomes/examples would improve impact and reduce redundancy.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a clear label and cleaner format: “Selected Recent Projects” with 1-line bullets instead of paragraph-style entries.
- Make each item more specific and parallel, e.g., start with a strong verb and emphasize scope or user value: “Led development of…,” “Built…,” “Produced…”
- Tighten wording: change “designed for continued campaign growth” to “built for future campaign expansion”; use “10 x 20-foot” for style consistency.
- Consider adding 1 concrete result where available (adoption, traffic, engagement, launch context) to strengthen impact.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series closely overlap with the current freelance role and NACo experience bullets.
- Anniversary campaign may be the best distinct example if it is not described elsewhere; prioritize unique projects here.

Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Core Competencies

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope and technical depth, but it reads as a service list rather than a results-oriented leadership entry. Tighten phrasing and foreground the highest-impact initiatives, especially AI search, Drupal campaign builds, and communications systems.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Lead digital strategy, campaign platform development, and content operations for a U.S. national membership organization.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/governance into one impact-focused line: “Built cross-functional workflows, analytics, and governance practices to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Rephrase technical execution more crisply: “Designed and launched Drupal-based campaign and storytelling experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- Elevate the standout initiative: “Spearheaded an AI-enabled search program, defining retrieval strategy, structured content requirements, and user-facing discovery experience.” Add metrics if possible: users served, time saved, pages improved, launch status.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating generic governance/analytics language already used in the NACo Director role.
- The Drupal microsite and AI search bullets overlap with Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and outcome-focused.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground enterprise outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget for a national association serving county officials.”
- Combine the website bullets and lead with the biggest outcome: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more outcome-based: add growth, engagement, open/click rates, production volume, cost savings, or turnaround improvements if available; otherwise trim “tens of thousands/thousands” language.
- Tighten ops/analytics bullets: “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio” and “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting to improve leadership visibility and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership, modernization, and infrastructure.
- Video-program expansion also appears in prior NACo roles; emphasize building the studio/capability, not recurring production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later NACo director role and earlier digital media role. Make it more distinct by emphasizing executional leadership, channel ownership, and any measurable growth or process improvements achieved before promotion.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to focus on scope and progression: “Directed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging prior to promotion to Director of Digital Media.”
- Tighten bullets and make outcomes explicit: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Strengthen the video bullet with impact if available: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine planning/workflow bullets into one sharper line: “Built cross-team editorial planning and publishing workflows that improved coordination among communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Improved digital publishing workflows” and “strengthened editorial planning” overlap with the Director role’s governance/planning bullets.
- Weekly video work also overlaps with the 2015–2018 role; keep this entry focused on scaling and formalizing the program.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent experience. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and public-sector specialization rather than generic content terms.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with more distinctive, outcome-oriented phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy for high-volume public-sector platforms
- Editorial governance and cross-functional publishing systems
- Multi-channel communications leadership across web, email, social and video
- Advocacy, policy and member-facing messaging strategy
- Consider dropping “Audience-focused content planning”; it reads junior compared with the rest of the CV.
- If space allows, use “content operations” instead of “content planning” to better match recent leadership roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” already appear almost verbatim in the header/Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; keep only one version across sections.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill mix, but this item is too tool-heavy and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and execution themes tied to recent Drupal modernization and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a software list to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS delivery • Website modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Put Drupal first and consider dropping WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages here unless central to target roles; they read as secondary versus recent enterprise Drupal work.
- Replace “CMS modernization” with “website modernization and migration” for clearer impact and alignment with the 10,000+ page Drupal migration.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: “AI-enabled search and discovery experiences” or “platform integrations and automation for editorial operations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT”; avoid repeating the same platform list in both sections.
- “Workflow automation” also overlaps with Core Competencies.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” Tighten it to emphasize strategic analytics capability, not just tool names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as outcomes-oriented: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity for analytics infrastructure, dashboarding and decision support”
- Replace generic “KPI design” with “KPI framework development” or “measurement strategy and KPI design”
- Tighten “Leadership reporting” to “executive reporting and performance dashboards”
- Consider revised line: “GA4 • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • Measurement strategy & KPI design • Executive dashboards • SEO and conversion/performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills more strategic and leave full tool inventory below.
- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating that exact phrasing.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it’s generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and multiple NACo bullets. Make it more senior and systems-focused, emphasizing production leadership rather than task-level execution.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as outcome-oriented capabilities, e.g.:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production
- Livestream and hybrid event production
- In-house studio buildout and operations
- PTZ camera and multi-camera production workflows
- Multimedia programming for advocacy and member communications
- Replace “Video production and editing” with “Broadcast-quality video production and post-production” to better match the studio/buildout achievement.
- Replace “Hybrid and virtual event production” with “Livestream and hybrid event production” for tighter phrasing and less repetition.
- If space allows, add one scale cue in the section heading or nearby summary, not here, such as “built in-house studio capacity.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the exact phrase.
- “Studio operations” and “video production” are already evidenced in recent NACo roles, so keep this list concise and differentiated.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Clear but too generic as a standalone skills line, and it overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Since Drupal is the strongest/recent platform, lead with it and add light proficiency context.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- If space allows, group by strength: Drupal • WordPress | SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- Consider dropping GitHub Pages unless it reflects meaningful recent use; it reads lighter than the rest.
- Keep this item platform-only; save modernization, integrations, and AI/search language for adjacent technical sections.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” under Topline Skills; consider removing one version or making this one shorter.
- “CMS modernization” already appears elsewhere, so don’t repeat it here.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Make it more current, implementation-focused, and selective.

Suggested edit
- Rename to emphasize applied capability: “Front-End Development & Technical Implementation” or “Web Development & Automation.”
- Tighten and group by relevance: “HTML5/CSS3, JavaScript/jQuery, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions.”
- If accurate, add scope or outcome in brief parentheticals, e.g., “API integrations (CMS/content workflows), Cloudflare Workers (edge scripting), GitHub Actions (deployment automation).”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless ATS targeting requires them; “HTML/CSS” is cleaner.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Strong overlap with Topline Skills [2] (“HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery,” “API integrations,” “Workflow automation”). Differentiate this item by focusing on tools actually used hands-on.
- GTM may fit better under analytics/measurement if that section already covers implementation tools.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems expertise. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools
- Reorder by relevance to recent work and group by function: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Trello • Basecamp
- If space allows, add light qualifiers to show depth, e.g. “Airtable (workflow databases), Power Automate, Zapier, Jira/Asana (project operations)”
- Best upgrade: replace the standalone list with outcome-oriented context elsewhere, e.g. “Built workflow automation and cross-team planning systems using Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira and Asana.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Slack,” “Teams,” “Trello,” and “Basecamp” are lower-value than the automation tools; consider trimming if space is tight.
- Avoid repeating “workflow automation” language already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The item is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this should stay tool-focused and avoid implying broad channel ownership again.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms
- Tighten the list to: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add one qualifier for level of use: Enterprise campaign automation, newsletter operations, and audience engagement
- If space allows, make platform names consistent with the rest of the CV by avoiding slashes: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights and Journeys

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding claims like “managed newsletters reaching tens of thousands” here; that impact is already stronger in the 2022–2024 and 2018–2022 experience entries.
- “Engagement” overlaps with broader multi-channel communications language elsewhere, so keep this item specifically about email/member platforms.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool set, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” In the Technical + IT section, it should read more like a concise tools list, with sharper phrasing and less conceptual language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Google Search Console • SEO analysis • Experimentation
- Swap “A/B testing” for “Experimentation” only if you’ve directly run tests; otherwise remove it to avoid overstating hands-on ownership.
- Replace “Dashboarding” with the actual platforms already listed; “dashboarding” is a function, not a tool.
- Add Google Search Console if used, since it makes the SEO claim more concrete and technical.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” Consider trimming one version or making this section tools-only while leaving KPI/reporting language in Topline Skills.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already substantiated in the 2022–2024 NACo role, so no need to repeat broader claims here.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize “firsts,” production volume, or workflow improvements from this earlier stage.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to stress foundational contribution: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital media function, supporting web, email, social, livestream and video operations.”
- Add concrete scope/results if available: website refresh size/timeline, number of livestreams or weekly videos produced, audience growth, email/social engagement, or workflow time saved.
- Tighten the management phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised one digital media associate,” if accurate.
- Possible version: “Promoted across two roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital media team. Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and improved cross-channel publishing workflows across web, email, social and multimedia while mentoring a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this as launching or early production rather than scaling.
- “Strengthening workflows” is repeated elsewhere; specify what changed or the channels/tools involved.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around outcomes or scope, while avoiding overlap with later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize the standout achievement first: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a clearer action: “Produced digital and multimedia content supporting program communications and policy outreach.”
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes, audience, internal stakeholders supported, or types of projects delivered.
- Keep this entry lighter than later NACo roles since digital leadership is covered more strongly from 2015 onward.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media positions; keep this item focused on innovation/research support plus the podcast launch.
- Avoid repeating video/livestream language already covered in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a mixed list of software and capabilities. It also overlaps with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and several work bullets, so it should be tightened to emphasize tools only.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Multimedia & Creative Software
- Rewrite as: Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator
- If you want to keep capabilities, split them into a separate skills line elsewhere: Livestream production • Studio operations • Podcast production
